topic.readerProblem: A marketer or founder keeps hearing that AI engines use RAG and grounding, but cannot tell what the terms mean, how they differ, or why they decide which pages get cited and what to change.
topic.connection: AEOeye audits whether ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Google AI and Perplexity name a brand; this guide explains the retrieve-then-generate mechanism behind those answers and connects it to crawler access, which AEOeye's own crawler access study measured.

assessment: The page defines RAG from the original 2020 paper and grounding from Google's own documentation, walks the retrieval pipeline step by step from vendor docs, and turns it into a retrievable-then-quotable checklist. It rests on vendor documentation, arXiv papers, Google's AI Overviews post, the Tow Center study and AEOeye's crawler access study, each with its scope stated. It deliberately does not claim how ChatGPT, Perplexity or Claude rank or chunk web pages internally (not public), does not claim a measured effect from our own page consolidation, and corrects the old advice to chunk content and add schema for AI.

sources.supports: Lewis et al. 2020 (Facebook AI Research, UCL, NYU): parametric plus non-parametric memory; Wikipedia split into 100-word chunks, 21M passages; more specific, diverse and factual output than a parametric-only baseline; BM25 performed best on entity-centric FEVER claims; index swap on 82 world leaders: 68% with matching 2018 index vs 4% with the 2016 index (read in the PDF text).
Definition of RAG as letting LLMs retrieve and incorporate new information from external data sources.

Google calls RAG a technique also known as grounding that retrieves pages from the Search index; query fan-out; eligibility (indexed, snippet-eligible, included in Search generative AI features in Search Console); no chunking requirement, no special schema, llms.txt ignored; unique point of view; scaled content abuse warning. Page last updated 2026-07-10.

Grounding defined as connecting model output to verifiable sources; reduces hallucinations, provides links to sources; RAG, Google Search and Google Maps listed as separate grounding types. Last updated 2026-10-01.
RAG stages: data ingestion, transformation (split into chunks), embedding, indexing, retrieval, generation; embeddings capture meaning so related text is close together.
Gemini grounding with Google Search: model decides whether a search can improve the answer, runs one or more queries, synthesizes results, returns inline citations. Last updated 2026-09-23.
Model can choose to search or not; inline citations by default; sources field lists all consulted URLs and is often longer than the citations list.
Moon-landing example (65% semantic similarity, 0% keyword overlap); default chunking 800 tokens with 400 overlap; score_threshold limits results to more relevant chunks.
Sites opted out of OAI-SearchBot will not be shown in ChatGPT search answers.
Claude searches for current or changing information and answers stable knowledge directly; search results include page_age (when the site was last updated).

Chunk 'The company's revenue grew by 3% over the previous quarter' lacks company and period; contextual embeddings cut top-20 retrieval failures 35% (5.7% to 3.7%), with contextual BM25 49% (to 2.9%). Published 2024-09-19.
Perplexity recommends allowing PerplexityBot; Perplexity-User generally ignores robots.txt because users initiate the fetch.
GEO benchmark: adding citations, quotations and statistics gave 30-40% relative gain on position-adjusted word count (PDF text); abstract says up to 40% and domain-dependent.
Crawling can take a few days to a few weeks; requesting a crawl does not guarantee inclusion. Last updated 2025-12-10.
Google's May 30, 2024 account: satirical content republished on a geological software provider's site, sarcastic forum content, and misreading of webpage language produced odd AI Overviews.
Liu, Zhang, Liang 2023: four engines (Bing Chat, NeevaAI, perplexity.ai, YouChat); 51.5% of sentences fully supported by citations, 74.5% of citations support their sentence.
Lost in the Middle (TACL 2023): performance often highest when relevant information is at the start or end of the context and degrades in the middle.

Tow Center, March 6, 2025: eight tools, 1,600 queries identifying the source of news excerpts, incorrect on more than 60%; USA Today blocks ChatGPT's crawler yet a syndicated Yahoo News copy was cited.
